tasks.short: Receive outage calls and request the appropriate personnel

steps.what: Receive outage calls and establish the immediate situation
Request necessary personnel according to the assessed outage and emergency arrangements

tasks.design: Keep outage assessment and personnel requests with the operator using {TELEPHONY} and the current emergency arrangements in {DOCS}. Native roster access can assist lookup, but no automatic classification or call-out is introduced without a demonstrated repeatable baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: The correct response depends on incomplete reports and changing plant conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated tool removes the operator's assessment and acknowledgement work.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing appropriate expertise and recognising escalation needs.
tasks.human_edge: Ask clarifying questions and confirm that a person has accepted the request.
tasks.altitude: The operator retains responsibility for incident communication.

reach.learn: Plant escalation arrangements and role responsibilities

evidence.claim: Outage assessment and personnel request conversations remain human in this scenario; no local saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary covers operator call reception, assessment and personnel requests; response personnel labour and outage repair are outside focal time.
No structured outage code, readiness flag or automatic dispatch is assumed. Existing roster and emergency arrangements remain human-maintained under the current process.
Native roster lookup is considered before custom software; existing communications runtime earns no new saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because no workflow change is proposed.
unknowns: Existing call-out system and roster ownership
Frequency of complex or ambiguous calls
research_questions: Is repeated roster lookup a distinct measurable burden after assessment and acknowledgement are counted?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=55+45=100, upkeep=0, net=0. Outage assessment and response requests remain human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Operate and monitor standby emergency generators

steps.what: Place standby emergency electrical generators on line under the authorised procedure
Monitor generator temperature, output and lubrication and respond to abnormal conditions

tasks.design: Keep generator operation and condition assessment with the operator using the plant-control {OTHER} and physical observations. Existing automatic starting sequences, protection and telemetry continue as installed and receive no new labour-saving credit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Emergency operation requires validated controls and situational judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated change removes operator checks or physical observation.
tasks.still_hard: Determining whether apparently normal readings conceal a developing fault.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise abnormal equipment behaviour and follow the authorised escalation procedure.

evidence.claim: Existing generator automation is not a new saving and does not remove the operator's condition assessment in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary covers human intervention and monitoring only; automatic controller runtime is excluded from focal-role baseline.
OTHER means the plant-control and generator instrumentation system. No new structured start permission, automatic switching command or inferred lubrication status is introduced.
Native controls remain under the existing validated configuration; no custom control software is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because no operating-system change is proposed.
unknowns: Required physical checks and operating authorisations
research_questions: Is there a separate reporting burden that can be measured without changing generator operation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+60=100, upkeep=0, net=0. Existing automatic runtime is outside the baseline and human checks are retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Inspect gas collection symptoms and relevant instrument trends
Diagnose gas collection problems and determine the next authorised investigation

tasks.design: Keep gas collection troubleshooting with the operator using historian and instrumentation {OTHER} alongside system documentation in {DOCS}. Existing alarms and trends assist diagnosis, but a new model-generated fault label does not replace inspection or causal reasoning.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different faults can produce similar readings, and some evidence is only available in the field.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated new tool removes this diagnostic effort for the specified system.
tasks.still_hard: Separating equipment, measurement and operating-condition causes.
tasks.human_edge: Test a hypothesis against physical evidence and recognise uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: The operator retains fault investigation responsibility.

reach.learn: Gas-system hazards and authorised diagnostic methods

evidence.claim: Gas collection diagnosis requires field evidence and contextual judgement; no task-level saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary ends with diagnostic findings and a next-investigation decision, excluding repair, switching and general well-field monitoring allocated separately.
OTHER means plant historian and instrumentation software. No new fault-code producer, machine diagnosis or automated control action is assumed.
Native trends and alarms remain available and receive no new labour-saving credit.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new tool or workflow is proposed.
unknowns: Collection-system design and available diagnostic measurements
research_questions: Is locating current system documentation a separate recurring burden that native search could reduce?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=55+45=100, upkeep=0, net=0. Inspection and causal diagnosis remain human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Monitor well fields through scheduled observations and instrument readings
Assess well-field functioning and performance against operating expectations

tasks.design: Keep periodic well-field observation and performance assessment with the operator, supported by instrumentation and historian {OTHER}. Existing telemetry and alarms continue; they do not establish that physical rounds or interpretive checks can be removed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Not every relevant field condition is represented by a sensor.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated new coverage or validation removes the required observation time.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting changes caused by collection conditions, instruments or the well field itself.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise the significance of conditions outside the telemetry.

reach.learn: Field-specific performance limits and observation requirements

evidence.claim: Digital rounds can feed a historian, as shown by AVEVA Mobile Operator; the digest provides no basis to remove this well-field's physical monitoring time.

assumptions: Boundary is periodic well-field monitoring and initial performance assessment, excluding fault diagnosis, repairs and operational-data report compilation.
OTHER means plant instrumentation and historian software. No new structured normal-status flag or automatic assessment is assumed; installed telemetry runtime remains outside human baseline.
Native trend and rounds facilities are considered before custom code. Any future removed round would require separate evidence about coverage, which is not assumed here.
Zero incremental upkeep because no workflow change is proposed.
unknowns: Required field observations and monitoring frequency
research_questions: Which required observations lack reliable telemetry, and how much human time is actually repeatable data transfer?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65+35=100, upkeep=0, net=0. Existing telemetry earns no new saving and required observation remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Outage communication, generator operation, gas troubleshooting and field assessment retain their human responsibilities.
reach: Coordinate outage personnel within existing arrangements
role.ambitious_version: An operator whose attention stays on plant conditions and accountable response, with existing automation credited only for what it already does.
